finding.observed_source_behavior: The pre-fix strict ClayCode validator credited mandatory bindings and omega commit/validation gates by raw substring occurrence anywhere in the completion. Therefore contract text in comments and required calls nested below control-flow depth were indistinguishable from the canonical top-level turn path for promotion scoring.
reproduced_bypass_classes: required binding text can be present only in a comment while satisfying the raw substring check
omega validation text can be present only in a comment while satisfying the raw substring check
required binding or omega validation calls can be nested under non-canonical control flow such as if false while satisfying the raw substring check
finding.correction: An earlier draft receipt/PR description named string-literal smuggling as a reproduced pre-fix bypass. That was too broad: quoted cfg/gate literals must be escaped inside a string and therefore do not preserve the exact raw substring. String-literal rejection remains a conservative defense test, but it is not claimed as the reproduced old exploit.
finding.risk: A completion could receive strict structural/OOD credit without expressing the required runtime binding or deterministic omega admission sequence on the canonical top-level path.
finding.repair: Count mandatory bindings, return, omega commit, omega gates, authority and generation only as standalone brace-depth-1 statements. Reject multiline/unclosed strings and comment syntax at this strict promotion boundary.
regressions_added: required binding inside string does not count as a statement
required binding inside comment fails closed

valid omega top-level gate sequence accepted
omega gate inside string does not count as a statement
omega gate inside comment fails closed
